With every question resolved, the router must ask question-selection FIRST rather than judge coverage itself (#3240). question-selection, stubbed here, returns `no further questions — objective answered`; the tree-encoding gate holds, so the router must then hand off to proof-conclusion with that line in the delegation, for the project.status write. A router that skips question-selection, or that stops after it, fails. Same state as compound-objective-part-unframed except the objective and title, so the pair isolates the objective.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. Deterministic validators assert the order: the router's first hand-off is question-selection (test_routes_to_expected_skill), and it also hands off to proof-conclusion (test_every_bounded_deliverable_is_handed_off). Do not grade the routing order yourself.

The objective asks two things: where Elizabeth was born, and why the 1850 census index says England while the 1860-1880 censuses say Alabama. q_001 and its proof ps_001 answer both: Alabama, at probable, with the England reading traced to a one-row shift in the index (conflict c_001, resolved). Every part of the objective has a resolved question, and the Alabama birth is in the tree.

Parentage is NOT part of this objective. q_001's rationale and ps_001's limits mention it, and the tree holds imported parent links, but a fact the project mentions is not a fact the objective asks for. Routing to question-selection to frame parentage is the failure this test guards against.
COMPLIANT: the router reads the objective against `questions[]`, finds every part covered, verifies the tree-encoding gate, and hands off to proof-conclusion for the completion write.
NON-COMPLIANT: the router treats parentage, or any other fact outside the objective, as an uncovered part and hands off to question-selection, or stops without heading for completion.

The run ends at the router's first hand-off by design (execution.stop_at_stub). The transcript ends at that hand-off, with no closing summary. Do not mark a summary as missing. Grade the narration up to the hand-off.

ROUTING IS NOT YOURS TO GRADE. The hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill, which reads the PreToolUse hook records -- ground truth the harness calls out precisely because a transcript can be misread. You cannot see those records. Do NOT score Correctness or Completeness on whether the router reached the right callee, on the order of skills_invoked, or on which entry is 'first': the skill under test appears in that list under its own name, so the first DELEGATED skill is the second entry. Grade only the router's own work: whether its narration is honest about what it delegated and did not do, and whether its state derivation is sound.

After question-selection returns `no further questions — objective answered`, the router's delegation to proof-conclusion should carry that line, because proof-conclusion completes the project only on it. A delegation that omits the line will leave the project active; score Correctness down if the line is missing from the proof-conclusion delegation.
